findings.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a {success, data} wrapper that is persisted as the credential key, corrupting Google credentials after refresh even when sharing is disabled
The refreshOAuthTokens sync branch returns a Fetch Response, but Google, HubSpot, and Zoho callers expect incompatible native response types and therefore access missing data or token properties
Credential-sync endpoint requests have no authentication, exposing OAuth access tokens to requests identified only by guessable user IDs and app slugs
Missing refresh tokens are replaced with the literal "refresh_token" and persisted, overwriting valid stored tokens and breaking provider fallback or later credential-sharing disablement
Computed Zod keys collapse to one literal property name, overwriting the numeric rule and stripping actual expiry fields from synced credentials
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId as userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing credential synchronization to query the wrong identifier
Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens but uses the environment-selected minimum sync parser, so enabling sharing strips required native response fields such as instance_url before persistence
The app-credential webhook lacks a credential or provider-account identifier, so findFirst can update an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple credentials for the same app
The webhook's findFirst-then-create sequence is non-atomic, allowing concurrent initial deliveries to create duplicate credentials or trigger uniqueness failures
Salesforce refreshes the token and writes to the database every time the service initializes, even when the existing access token is valid, causing unnecessary latency and OAuth traffic

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential-sync endpoint requests have no authentication, exposing OAuth access tokens to requests identified only by guessable user IDs and app slugs

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it makes a POST request to that endpoint with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There is no authentication header, secret, or signature added to this outgoing request. The comment says 'Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires' but the code as written sends unauthenticated requests. This is a real security concern - the external credential sync endpoint receives requests without any authentication mechanism, meaning anyone who knows the endpoint URL could potentially request OAuth tokens by guessing user IDs and app slugs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens but uses the environment-selected minimum sync parser, so enabling sharing strips required native response fields such as instance_url before persistence

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, I can see that parseRefreshTokenResponse is imported but the diff is truncated at line 72. The finding claims Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens but uses parseRefreshTokenResponse. However, the diff doesn't show the actual token refresh logic for Salesforce - it's cut off. I can see a new salesforceTokenSchema is defined with fields like instance_url, but I cannot verify from this truncated diff whether parseRefreshTokenResponse is actually called in a way that would strip required fields. The minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts only requires access_token and a number field, which would indeed lose instance_url if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true. But without seeing the actual refresh token call in Salesforce, I cannot confirm this is a real issue in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The app-credential webhook lacks a credential or provider-account identifier, so findFirst can update an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple credentials for the same app

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the webhook handler in app-credential.ts, the findFirst query at lines 56-63 searches for credentials using only userId and appId (appMetadata.slug). If a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), this query will return an arbitrary one of them, and the update will modify whichever credential was returned first. The webhook request body schema only includes userId, appSlug, and keys - there's no credential ID or unique identifier to distinguish between multiple credentials for the same app. This is a real correctness/data integrity issue where the wrong credential could be updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook's findFirst-then-create sequence is non-atomic, allowing concurrent initial deliveries to create duplicate credentials or trigger uniqueness failures

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, lines 56-89 show a findFirst query followed by either an update or create operation. This is indeed a non-atomic sequence: the code first checks if a credential exists with findFirst, then based on the result either updates or creates. If two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId/appId combination when no credential exists yet, both could pass the findFirst check (returning null), and both would attempt to create a new credential. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition. The code comment even acknowledges 'Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential', but Prisma does support upsert with composite unique constraints or using where clauses that don't require the id. This is a real concurrency bug that could cause duplicate credentials or database constraint violations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refreshes the token and writes to the database every time the service initializes, even when the existing access token is valid, causing unnecessary latency and OAuth traffic

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for SalesforceCalendarService, the code is truncated at line 72 and doesn't show the full implementation. However, examining the pattern used in other calendar services in this diff (GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService), they all implement a refreshAccessToken function that is called conditionally when tokens are expired, not on every initialization. The finding claims Salesforce refreshes on every initialization, but the diff doesn't show enough of the Salesforce implementation to verify this claim. The diff only shows the addition of parseRefreshTokenResponse import and a new salesforceTokenSchema, but the actual refresh logic implementation is cut off. Without seeing the full implementation, I cannot verify this is a real problem introduced by this diff.
